game:item-handbooktext-scrapings-*: Scrapings require multiple stages of processing, distilling and mixing to become useable, but are effectively duplicated in the process! Scrapings first need to be mixed in a barrel with clean water. The resulting slurry must be processed further in a boiler to seperate solid waste from the useable liquids. Depending on which type of scraping was used you'll have melted resin, melted rendered fat or lubricant. Melted resin and rendered fat need time to cool and coagulate in a barrel before being further processed. After they have congealed, the semi-solid fluid can be processed back into their respective items, or in the case of lubricant, used elsewhere.

game:sdr-recycling-text:
Recycling

Want not, waste not.

Over time you'll amass more items, blocks and resources, but some of them may no longer be of use. Perhaps you finished a building project and have some roofs to spare, or have outgrown reed baskets for storage, or maybe just made one barrel too many. Thanks to the power of recycling most of these can be broken down into either their base components or into a different useful resource.

Methods
Depending on what you intend to recycle the method can vary: in this the handbook is your friend! Simply navigating to the item's page will show what resources it can be broken into. (typically under the 'Ingredient for' text) Items can be recycled through these mediums:

Crafting Grid: Used for just about everything, simply place the desired item and the appropriate tool in the grid to recycle.

Barrels: Decompose rotting wood and organic blocks into rot. Can also disolve certain blocks into various mixtures.

Firepits: Burning any wooden items containing bits of metal or glass allows you to reclaim 100% of that material in exchange for destroying all the wood.

Crucible: Some smaller metal items like tool heads and lamellae can be melted inside a crucible without losing any material or requiring a bloomery.

Bloomeries: Allows melting of any metal item too large to fit in a crucible, along with the same 100% return rate on material.

(Only items that have 'Smelts into' under their smelting temperature can be melted in crucibles and bloomeries)

Using the Right Tools
When recycling an item in the crafting grid it will yeild roughly 50% of each ingredient used to make it. Depending on the item's ingredients different tools may be required. Items made out of sticks and logs typically need an axe to be broken down, while something made of boards may require the use of a saw.

Note: Items made with multiple resources will only show a single output in the handbook, but will still give you each ingredient.
game:gamemechanicinfo-panning-text:
Panning
There's gold in those hills!

Panning allows the player to obtain small quantities of copper and a few other types of nuggets, as well as other items. It is a useful way to obtain copper nuggets in the early game, if you're not finding enough through exploring.

All the player needs for panning are a wooden pan, water to stand in, and either sand, gravel, or bony soil (muddy gravel will NOT work). Simply stand in the water, rightmouse click the pan on the material to be sifted, and then rightmouse click once to start sifting. Each block of material has eight 'charges' for the pan.

The stone type of sand and gravel makes no difference in results, aside form the stones that you obtain from it. Sand and gravel produce the same results. Bony soil, however, will produce a much different set of results from sand and gravel.

All types of soil, including soil adjacent blocks such as strewn straw and cob, can be panned for various seeds, organic materials and other goodies. The higher the fertility, the higher the chances of yeilding rare items. Panning soil will not produce any ore nuggets.
game:block-handbooktext-anvil-*: Anvils can be broken down into ingots using a chisel. This will require an amount of chisel durability equal to the full new durability of a chisel of the same metal tier as the anvil. However, scrapping with a chisel will only yeild half of the total metal. Smelt down the anvil in a bloomery to recieve the full metal cost.
